summary.title: Build a static site generator in 40 lines with Node.js
summary.one_liner: You learn how to write a minimal static site generator in Node.js that renders EJS pages into a shared layout and writes HTML to a public folder, then extend it with Markdown, front matter and multiple layouts.
takeaways: A static site generator can be built from a small script that globs page templates, renders them with EJS, wraps them in a layout and writes HTML to a public folder.
Site-wide config and JSON data files are loaded once and injected into every template render.
Markdown support can be added with marked, and per-page metadata with front-matter.
Per-page layouts can be chosen through a front matter layout attribute.
summary.summary: The author explains why they built a small custom static site generator instead of using Jekyll, Hugo or Hexo, which they found had too many features for a simple portfolio site. The core generator is a single scripts/build.js file of about 40 lines that uses ejs, fs-extra and glob, with promisified callbacks, to empty the output folder, copy assets, and render each page and then the layout. Bonus sections add Markdown and front matter via marked and front-matter, and multiple layouts selected per page, and the post closes with ideas such as live reload, deploys and asset preprocessing.
